paper.title: Online SuBmodular + SuPermodular (BP) Maximization with Bandit Feedback

settings.name_in_paper: Interactive BP / weakly submodular maximization with monolithic noisy marginal-gain feedback (GP contextual bandit)
unmapped: Each of m set functions h_q (BP: monotone submodular + monotone supermodular, or weakly submodular) is incrementally built by choosing one new item per arrival; reward is the marginal gain h_q(v|S)
Marginal gain function Delta(phi,S,v) lies in an RKHS with norm <= B (known to tune beta_t)
Regret is alpha-regret against alpha times the optimal size-T_q set per context, alpha depending on curvatures / submodularity ratio
Order of context arrivals not specified
settings.definition_quote: The optimizer encounters one of $m$ set functions from the set $\{h_1 \ldots h_m \}$ ... Monolithic Feedback: The optimizer receives $y_\tvar$ with $y_\tvar = h_{u_\tvar} (v_\tvar| S_{t_{u_\tvar}, u_\tvar}) + \epsilon_\tvar$.

settings.name_in_paper: Interactive BP maximization with separate feedback
unmapped: Separate noisy feedback for the submodular part f and supermodular part g of the BP function
Learner knows T_q (number of items per user) and possibly the modular lower bound l_{q,1}
RKHS norm bound B on the marginal gain function
settings.definition_quote: Separate Feedback: In the BP case, pair $(y_{f, \tvar},y_{g, \tvar})$ may be available with $y_{f, \tvar} = f_{u_\tvar} (v_\tvar| S_{t_{u_\tvar}, u_\tvar}) + \epsilon_\tvar/2$ and $y_{g, \tvar} = g_{u_\tvar} (v_\tvar| S_{t_{u_\tvar}, u_\tvar}) + \epsilon_\tvar/2$.

symbols.B_rkhs: RKHS norm bound on the marginal-gain function Delta

conditions: Delta lies in RKHS with norm <= B (Assumption 1)
tuning: beta_t = sqrt(lambda) B + sqrt(4 log T + log(e + e t/lambda) d_eff)

source.label: thm:bp_regret_bound
source.quote: When all $h_q$ are BP functions, we have that $\mathbb{E} [\mathcal{R}_{\text{BP}}(\Tvar)] \leq O\left(\sqrt{\Tvar} \left(B \sqrt{\lambda \deff} + \deff\right) \right)$

results.notes: Expected alpha-regret with alpha = (1/kappa_f)[1-exp(-(1-kappa^g)kappa_f)] per context; quantity set to other since it is a scaled combinatorial regret. Comparator is alpha times optimal set per context.

symbols.B_rkhs: RKHS norm bound on the marginal-gain function Delta

conditions: all h_q are weakly submodular (submodularity ratio gamma_q, generalized curvature zeta_q)
Delta lies in RKHS with norm <= B (Assumption 1)
tuning: beta_t = sqrt(lambda) B + sqrt(4 log T + log(e + e t/lambda) d_eff)

source.label: thm:bp_regret_bound
source.quote: When all $h_q$ are WS functions, we have that $\mathbb{E} [\mathcal{R}_{\text{WS}}(\Tvar)] \leq O\left(\sqrt{\Tvar} \left(B \sqrt{\lambda \deff} + \deff\right) \right)$

symbols.B_rkhs: RKHS norm bound on the marginal-gain function Delta

conditions: Assumption 2: modular lower bound l_{q,1} known, separate feedback oracles, T_q known

source.label: thm:bp_regret_bound_dist_strong
source.quote: Let Assumptions~\ref{ass:rkhs} and \ref{ass:separate} hold and assume that $\epsilon_\tvar$ are i.i.d centered sub-Gaussian noise. Then, when all $h_q$ are BP functions, Algorithm~\ref{alg:mnnucb_dist} yields \[ \mathbb{E}[\mathcal{R}_{\text{BP}, 2} (\Tvar)] \leq O\left(\sqrt{\Tvar} \left(B \sqrt{\lambda \deff} + \deff\right) \right) \]

symbols.B_rkhs: RKHS norm bound on the marginal-gain function Delta

source.label: prop:bp_regret_bound_dist_weaker
source.quote: Let Assumption~\ref{ass:rkhs} and \ref{assump:1.2} and \ref{assump:1.3} hold. Additionally, let the conditions on $\epsilon_\tvar$ hold as in Theorem~\ref{thm:bp_regret_bound_dist_strong}. Then Algorithm~\ref{alg:mnnucb_dist} with the modification above yields $ \mathbb{E} [\mathcal{R}_{\text{BP, 3}} (\Tvar)] \leq O\left(\sqrt{\Tvar} \left(B \sqrt{\lambda \deff} + \deff\right) \right)$
